links.comparator_used: Strict three-domain gate requirements versus a validated partial-observation extension (no ungated comparator reported)
links.outcome: Proportion of visits at which governed forecasts were released, and the reasons for suppression
links.effect: Released at 32.7% of visits under strict three-domain requirements, rising to 48.1% under the partial-observation extension. Suppression was driven by incomplete clinical assessment (51.5%) rather than model uncertainty (0.2%). It was equitable across sexes (Cramér's V=0.049).
links.tradeoff: Most visits had forecasts suppressed under strict requirements, mainly because of incomplete assessments, so fewer forecasts are available to clinicians.
links.quote: The confidence gate released governed forecasts at 32.7% of visits under strict three-domain requirements, increasing to 48.1% under a validated partial-observation extension.

links.outcome: Coverage of 95% predictive intervals across MDS-UPDRS III, MoCA and SCOPA-AUT
links.effect: 94% to 96% coverage for the Bayesian model with full posterior uncertainty, versus 64–69% for linear mixed-effects baselines
links.quote: Predictive interval coverage at the 95% level ranged from 94% to 96% across all three endpoints, compared with 64–69% for linear mixed-effects baselines.

design_hint: uncertainty-gated reporting (confidence gate suppressing unreliable forecasts)
